A few commenters added that children whose families receive housing assistance are more likely to have a healthy weight, improved mental health outcomes, educational gains in math and language arts, and higher earning and educational attainment, along with a lower chance of incarceration in adulthood. Some referenced a study that found that in households where caregivers reported receipt of heat or energy assistance, children had healthier weights and lower rates of acute hospitalization.
回应:就评论人士认为本规则应对住房不稳定和无家可归负责而言,国土安全部指出,本规则并未指示外国人放弃申请或领取其有资格获得的、用于解决住房不稳定和无家可归问题的按经济状况核发的公共福利。如果某外国人领取了此类按经济状况核发的公共福利,那是因为该外国人提出了申请,并经福利提供机构认定符合领取资格。
Response: To the extent the commenters believe this rule would be responsible for housing instability and homelessness, DHS notes the rule does not instruct aliens to forgo applying for or receiving means-tested public benefits that address housing instability and homelessness for which they are eligible. If an alien received such means-tested public benefits, it is because the alien applied for and was determined eligible for those benefits by the benefit providing agency.
此外,正如拟议规则制定通知(NPRM)中所讨论的,国土安全部评估了本规则对儿童的影响,并认定本规则可能对儿童(包括美国公民儿童)的健康和教育机会产生负面影响。国土安全部认为,通过就最终规则的适用方式以及公共负担不可入境事由认定如何在综合考量情况下运作进行明确沟通,可以缓解部分此类潜在影响。然而,国土安全部最终仍然认为,儿童所受的任何影响,均被与本规则制定相关的令人信服的法律和政策理由所超越,这些理由包括但不限于更好地确保自给自足。国土安全部的意图是落实国会的授权,即根据《移民与国籍法》第212(a)(4)(A)条(8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(A)),评估外国人是否已履行其举证责任,证明其在任何时候都不太可能成为公共负担,这是鉴于国会的政策旨在确保前来美国的人应当自给自足,而不应依赖政府援助来满足其需求。
Additionally, as discussed in the NPRM, DHS assessed the rule's effect on children and determined that the rule may negatively impact the health and education opportunities for children, including U.S. citizen children. DHS believes that some of these potential impacts could be mitigated by clear communication regarding the application of the final rule and how the public charge inadmissibility determinations work in the totality of the circumstances. Ultimately, however, DHS continues to believe that any impact on children is outweighed by the compelling legal and policy reasons associated with this rulemaking, including but not limited to, better ensuring self-sufficiency. DHS's intent is to implement Congress's mandate to assess whether an alien has met his or her burden to demonstrate that he or she is not likely at any time to become a public charge under section 212(a)(4)(A) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(A), given the congressional policy to ensure those coming to the United States should be self-sufficient and not rely on the government for assistance to meet their needs.
美国国土安全部（DHS）还指出，是国会而非国土安全部，既允许某些特定类别的外国人领取经济状况调查类公共福利，又使这些相同的外国人受到公共负担可予拒绝入境理由的约束。尽管外国人可能会因为领取其有资格获得的经济状况调查类公共福利会如何影响其获得移民利益的资格，而重新考虑是否领取此类福利，但本规则并不禁止外国人领取国会使其有资格获得的任何公共福利。
DHS also notes Congress, not DHS, both permitted certain limited categories of aliens to receive means-tested public benefits and subjected the same aliens to the public charge ground of inadmissibility. Although aliens may reconsider receiving means-tested public benefits for which they are eligible due to how it impacts their eligibility for immigration benefits, this rule does not prohibit aliens from receiving any public benefit for which Congress made them eligible.
如《拟议规则制定通知》（NPRM）中所述，在确定申请入境或身份调整的外国人在任何时候成为公共负担的可能性时，国土安全部根据管辖性判例，综合考虑法定最低限度因素以及与评估申请人在任何时候成为公共负担可能性相关的所有其他信息的整体情况，包括该外国人领取经济状况调查类公共福利的情况。90 FR 52168, 52188 (2025年11月19日)。《移民与国籍法》（INA）第212(a)(4)(B)条和第212(s)条，8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(B)和1182(s)。
As noted in the NPRM, in determining whether an alien applying for admission or adjustment of status is likely at any time to become a public charge, DHS considers the statutory minimum factors and all other information relevant to assessing an applicant's likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge in the totality of the circumstances, including the alien's receipt of means-tested public benefits, consistent with governing precedent. 90 FR 52168, 52188 (Nov. 19, 2025). INA secs. 212(a)(4)(B) and 212(s), 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(B) and 1182(s).
评论意见：少数评论者表示担忧，家长会因担心危及移民身份而让子女退出启蒙计划（Head Start）等幼儿教育项目。另有评论者指出，早期教育和儿童保育项目有助于儿童发展，提高入学准备和学业表现，同时也支持正在工作或求学的家长。为进一步说明启蒙计划的益处，少数评论者指出，启蒙计划的参与者在成年后受教育程度更高，被监禁的可能性更低，依赖公共援助的可能性也更低。一位评论者描述了儿童保育与发展整笔拨款（CCDBG）等项目的重要性，表示CCDBG有助于家长负担优质的儿童保育费用，如果没有这些服务，家庭将在参与劳动力市场和将子女置于不理想的照护环境之间做出艰难抉择，并预计尽管许多家庭的美国公民子女符合资格，这些家庭仍会放弃通过CCDBG获得的照护服务。一个组织评论称，该规则将造成损害，因为与贫困相关的状况，包括未经治疗的身体和心理健康需求，可能会被儿童福利机构误判为忽视儿童。
Comment: A few commenters expressed concern that parents would withdraw children from early childhood education programs such as Head Start for fear of jeopardizing immigration status. Others remarked that early education and child care programs support child development and improve school readiness and academic performance while supporting parents who work and pursue education. Further describing the benefits of Head Start, a few commenters remarked Head Start participants have improved educational attainment, are less likely to be incarcerated, and less likely to depend on public assistance as adults. One commenter described the importance of programs such as the Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG), saying that CCDBG helps parents afford quality child care, and without access to these services, families face difficult decisions about participating in the workforce or leaving children in suboptimal care settings, anticipating that many families would forgo care through the CCDBG, despite their U.S. citizen children being eligible. One organization commented the rule would be detrimental because poverty-related conditions, including untreated health and mental health needs, may be mischaracterized as neglect by child welfare agencies.
少数评论者表示担忧，该规则将降低家庭使用早期干预（EI）项目的意愿和能力，因为尚不清楚参加早期干预服务是否会被纳入公共负担可予拒绝入境认定的范围。另有评论者对州级经济资助是否可能被纳入公共负担可予拒绝入境认定范围表示担忧，并警告称这将阻碍移民或美国公民子女接受高等教育。
A few commenters expressed concerns the rule would reduce families' willingness and ability to use early intervention (EI) programs because it was unclear if enrollment in EI services would be included in the scope of a public charge inadmissibility determination. Others expressed concerns of confusion regarding whether State-based financial aid could be considered in the scope of a public charge inadmissibility determination, warning that this would deter immigrants or U.S. citizen children from pursuing higher education.
一个专业医疗保健组织表示担忧，拟议规则将导致不确定性和困惑，使患有肾病的儿童家庭不敢获取其所需的关键医疗护理。
A professional healthcare organization expressed concern that the proposed rule would lead to uncertainty and confusion, deterring families from accessing critical medical care needed for children with kidney disease.
多位评论者描述了支持儿童项目所带来的长期经济和健康效益。一场格式信函活动和一位评论者指出，营养项目是对社区健康、福祉和发展的投资，妇女、婴儿和儿童特别补充营养计划（WIC）每花费1美元，估计可在医疗、教育和生产力方面节省2.48美元，并得出结论称“拟议规则将逆转数十年来在减少饥饿和贫困方面取得的进展，导致一个更加饥饿、更加病弱、更加贫穷的国家”。
Multiple commenters described the long-term economic and health benefits of programs supporting children. A form letter campaign and a commenter stated nutrition programs are an investment in the health, well-being, and development of communities, with every $1 spent on Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) generating an estimated $2.48 in medical, educational, and productivity savings, concluding “the proposed rule would reverse decades of progress in reducing hunger and poverty, leading to a hungrier, sicker, and poorer nation.”
评论者引用研究表明,儿童获得公共健康保险和医疗补助(Medicaid)的机会改善了健康结果并降低了政府支出,其中包括一项研究显示,幼儿期获得食品券(food stamps)在教育、收入、住房所有权、社区质量和预期寿命方面产生了显著改善,每投入一美元可为社会带来62美元的效益。另一位评论者解释说,诸如启蒙计划(Head Start)之类的早期教育项目能够减少(印刷页45365)违法行为和犯罪。另一位评论者写道,随着注册医疗补助的学生减少,学校获得的用于支付健康服务和人员费用的资金也会减少。一位评论者指出,由于需要为没有医疗保健或食品援助机会的儿童提供服务,并增加对特殊教育服务和校医的支出,州政府的支出将会增加。
Commenters cited research showing children's access to public health insurance and Medicaid improved health outcomes and reduced government costs, including a study showing that access to food stamps in early childhood produced significant improvements in education, income, home ownership, neighborhood quality, and life expectancy, with every dollar invested generating $62 in societal benefits. A different commenter explained that early education programs such as Head Start result in reduced ( printed page 45365) delinquency and crime. Another wrote that with fewer students enrolled in Medicaid, the amount of funding schools receive to pay for health services and staff decreases. One commenter stated that State expenditures would increase due to the need to provide services to children without medical care or access to food assistance, and more spending on special education services and school nurses.
评论者指出,早期教育项目的运营利润微薄,依靠入学率来维持开放、留住员工并保持质量,其中一位评论者认为该规则将阻碍家庭获取这些资源,降低入学率,使资金不稳定,并加速项目关闭。另一些人写道,该规则将对儿童在课堂上学习的能力产生负面影响。不同的评论者指出,学校食品项目的更高参与度通过增加联邦收入来增强项目财务状况,产生规模经济效应,从而降低准备和提供餐食的成本。另一些人指出,在学校营养支持项目中使用直接资格认定(direct certification)可以减少individual家庭的文书工作、未付餐费债务,以及为确定报销等级而需要清点和记录每份所供餐食的需要,从而为地方和联邦资源节省开支。
Commenters remarked that early education programs operate on thin margins and rely on enrollment to stay open, retain staff, and maintain quality, with one suggesting the rule would discourage families from accessing these resources, reduce enrollment, destabilize funding, and accelerate program closures. Others wrote that the rule would negatively impact children's ability to learn in the classroom. Different commenters stated that higher participation in school food programs strengthens program finances by increasing Federal revenues, generating economies of scale that reduce the cost of preparing and serving meals. Others stated the use of direct certification for eligibility in nutrition support programs in schools reduce individual family paperwork, unpaid meal debt, and the need to count and document each meal served to determine what tier of reimbursement they qualify for and in turn saves local and Federal resources.
回应:本规则恢复了评估所有相关事实的广泛裁量权,并与长期以来的政策保持一致,即在美国的外国人应自力更生,政府福利不应成为移民的激励因素。本规则并不妨碍任何有资格获得基于经济状况审查的公共福利的外国人申请或领取此类福利。国土安全部(DHS)正在执行《个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)中国会的指示,即在美国的外国人不应依赖公共资源来满足其需求。DHS认为,2022年最终规则未能忠实执行PRWORA以及《移民与国籍法》(INA)第212(a)(4)(A)条,8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(A),因为该规则通过限制DHS官员在综合考量所有情况时可以考虑哪些公共福利,以及阻止官员考虑规则中列出的七项因素之外的其他因素,束缚了DHS官员的裁量权。通过本最终规则,DHS旨在更好地确保申请人自给自足。DHS还指出,公共负担不可入境事由并不适用于所有申请签证、入境或身份调整的申请人。国会根据INA第207(c)(3)条和第209(c)条,8 U.S.C. 1157(c)(3)、1159(c),专门豁免了某些群体,例如在入境和身份调整时的难民和庇护获准者。
Response: This rule restores broad discretion to evaluate all pertinent facts and aligns with long-standing policy that aliens in the United States should be self-reliant and government benefits should not incentivize immigration. It does not prevent any alien eligible for means-tested public benefits from applying for or receiving benefits. DHS is implementing the congressional directive in PRWORA that aliens in the United States should not depend on public resources to meet their needs. DHS believes the 2022 Final Rule did not faithfully implement PRWORA and section 212(a)(4)(A) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(A), insofar as they straitjacketed DHS officers by limiting what public benefits DHS can consider in the totality of the circumstances and by precluding officers from considering factors beyond the seven outlined in the rule. Through this final rule, DHS seeks to better ensure applicants are self-sufficient. DHS also notes that the public charge inadmissibility ground does not apply to all applicants who are seeking a visa, admission, or adjustment of status. Congress specifically exempted certain groups, e.g., refugees and asylees at the time of admission and adjustment of status, pursuant to sections 207(c)(3) and 209(c) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1157(c)(3), 1159(c).
二、对身份混合家庭的影响
ii. Impacts on Mixed Status Families
评论:评论者描述了拟议规则的退出登记效应将对移民社区产生的总体影响,包括贫困率上升、住房不稳定、饥饿以及不良健康结果。另一些人指出,该规则将在身份混合家庭中造成恐惧、困惑或不确定性,并阻止符合条件的美国公民和合法永久居民(LPR)获取福利。另一位评论者指出,获得豁免的群体可能与未获豁免的移民共同生活,因担心危及他人的移民身份而回避使用公共服务。众多评论者指出,拟议规则将使家庭担心家庭成员(包括美国公民子女)所获得的服务和福利会在公共负担评估中被不利地考虑,从而导致家庭放弃福利和医疗照护。少数评论者认为,拟议规则的寒蝉效应将对美国公民子女造成最严重的影响,因为作为公民,他们目前有资格获得范围最广的公共服务。
Comment: Commenters described general impacts the proposed rule's disenrollment effect would have on immigrant communities, including increased rates of poverty, housing instability, hunger, and poor health outcomes. Others stated that the rule would foster fear, confusion, or uncertainty in mixed-status households and deter access to benefits among eligible U.S. citizens and LPRs. Another noted that exempt populations may live with non-exempt immigrants and avoid public services out of fear of jeopardizing others' immigration status. Numerous commenters, stated the proposed rule would cause families to worry that services and benefits received by family members, including U.S. citizen children, would be held against them in a public charge assessment, leading families to forgo benefits and care. A few commenters reasoned that the chilling effect of the proposed rule would fall hardest on U.S. citizen children, since, as citizens, they are currently eligible for the widest range of public services.
评论者指出,删除关于家庭成员领取福利不被视为“领取”的明确说明,使移民无法确定家庭成员使用福利是否会在其申请合法永久居民身份时对其造成不利影响,而服务提供者也更难向其提供有意义的建议或保证。他们提及诸如补充营养援助计划(SNAP)、医疗补助(Medicaid)、儿童健康保险计划(CHIP)和妇女、婴儿及儿童特别营养补充计划(WIC)等项目的参与率,在2019年时,公民子女且父母为外国人的家庭的参与率下降幅度,远高于仅有美国公民的家庭。评论者援引城市研究所(Urban Institute)的调查结果指出,在那段时期,移民家庭中有未成年子女的成年人中,近四分之三不了解其子女参与公共福利计划不会被计入对其父母的公共负担不可入境性认定中。
Commenters stated removing the explicit clarification that benefits on behalf of family members was not considered “receipt,” leaves immigrants unable to determine whether the use of benefits by family members would harm them when seeking LPR status, and providers are less able to offer them meaningful advice or reassurance. They referenced participation in programs like SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP, and WIC, which declined at much higher rates for citizen children with aliens parents than for households with only U.S. citizens in 2019. Citing survey results from the Urban Institute, commenters remarked that during that time, nearly three quarters of adults in immigrant families with children did not understand that their children's participation in public benefits programs would not be considered in parents' public charge inadmissibility determinations.
在讨论对删除“领取”定义的担忧时,许多评论者引用了研究、学术成果或轶事证据,描述了与此删除相关的潜在寒蝉效应。评论者提供了证据,说明2019年最终规则发布后,包括患有残疾的美国公民子女在内的符合资格个人在医疗保健、SNAP、医疗补助、CHIP和WIC领取方面出现了寒蝉效应。评论者还表达了对慢性病患者、残疾人士、老年人、照护者及护理工作人员所受寒蝉影响的担忧,认为其结果与公共卫生目标背道而驰。他们表示,移民照护者可能担心其符合资格的家庭成员使用医疗补助居家及社区服务(HCBS)会被视为照护者本人领取公共福利。评论者警告称,删除“领取”的定义将产生一定程度的模糊性,导致移民身份混合的家庭从联邦资助的住房中自行迁出,从而加剧不稳定性,并在健康、教育和就业方面产生不良后果。评论者要求国土安全部(DHS)在法规和指南中明确保证,家庭成员使用公共福利不会被用于对申请人作出公共负担不可入境性认定的不利认定,或者此类福利的领取在权重上应低于申请人本人领取的情形。
While discussing concerns with the removal of the definition of “receipt,” many commenters cited research, studies, or anecdotal evidence describing potential chilling effects associated with the removal. Commenters shared evidence of chilling effects after the publication of the 2019 Final Rule on healthcare, SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP, and WIC receipt among eligible individuals, including U.S. citizen children with disabilities. Commenters also articulated concerns on chilling impacts for individuals with chronic diseases, people with disabilities, older adults, caregivers, and care workers, with outcomes running counter to public health goals. They stated that immigrant caregivers may be concerned their eligible family member's use of Medicaid home and community based services (HCBS) would be considered receipt of public benefits for the caregiver themselves. Commenters cautioned removing the definition of “receipt” would create a level of ambiguity that would lead families with mixed immigration status to self-evict from federally subsidized homes, leading to increased instability and poor outcomes in health, education, and employment. Commenters requested DHS provide explicit assurances in the regulations and guidance use of public benefits by a family member will not be held against applicants in a public charge inadmissibility determination or receipt of such benefits carry less weight than if the applicant received them.
答复:国土安全部感谢评论者就取消“(公共福利的)领取”定义可能导致符合资格领取公共福利的个人退出登记或放弃登记的情况表达关切。本规则不适用于美国公民及被豁免适用公共负担不可入境性条款的外国人。国土安全部承认,受公共负担不可入境性条款约束且育有美国公民子女的外国人,可能为避免本最终规则带来的不利后果,而拒绝为其符合资格的子女登记参加经济状况调查型公共福利计划。然而,国土安全部拒绝保留2022年最终规则中的此项定义或其他任何定义。国土安全部同时承认2019年最终规则所产生的寒蝉效应,但尽管该规则更贴近《移民与国籍法》(INA)第212(a)(4)条,即8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4),以及《个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)背后的国会立法意图,该规则也规定了一套僵化且复杂的监管体系,不必要地限制了官员的自由裁量权。国土安全部正在发布对2022年最终规则所有内容的彻底废止,公共负担保证金条款除外,该条款将在本规则中予以修订。
Response: DHS thanks the commenters for expressing concerns about how the elimination of the definition of “receipt (of public benefits)” may increase disenrollment or foregone enrollment by individuals eligible to receive public benefits. This rule does not apply to U.S. citizens and aliens exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility. DHS acknowledges aliens subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility who have U.S. citizen children may decline to enroll their children in means-tested public benefit programs for which their children are eligible in order to avoid negative consequences as a result of this final rule. However, DHS declines to retain this or any other definition from the 2022 Final Rule. DHS also acknowledges the chilling effects of the 2019 Final Rule but, while closer to congressional intent behind section 212(a)(4) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4), and PRWORA, that rule also prescribed a rigid and complex regulatory scheme that unnecessarily constrained officer discretion. DHS is publishing a clean rescission of all elements of the 2022 Final Rule other than the public charge bond provisions, which it is amending in this rule.
本规则既不改变领取经济状况调查型公共福利的资格,也未表明符合该福利资格的个人不应领取该福利。如果外国人已领取经济状况调查型公共福利,那是因为该外国人已向提供福利的机构提出申请,并经该机构认定符合资格。是国会,而非国土安全部,设立了这样一个框架:某些外国人既符合领取经济状况调查型公共福利的资格(印刷页45366),又受公共负担不可入境性条款的约束。
This rule neither alters eligibility to receive means-tested public benefits, nor states that an individual who is eligible for those benefits should not receive those benefits. If an alien has received means-tested public benefits, it is because the alien applied for and was determined eligible for those benefits by the benefit providing agency. Congress, not DHS, created a framework where certain aliens are both eligible for ( printed page 45366) means-tested public benefits and subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility.
如申请前规则制定通知(NPRM)中所述,在确定外国人在任何时候成为公共负担的可能性时,国土安全部(DHS)将考虑法定最低限度因素以及与评估申请人在任何时候成为公共负担可能性相关的所有其他信息,综合考虑全部情况,包括是否领取任何经济状况调查型公共福利,这与现行判例保持一致。见90 FR 52168, 52188(2025年11月19日)。移民与国籍法(INA)第212(a)(4)(B)条和第212(s)条,8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(B)和1182(s)。
As noted in the NPRM, in determining whether an alien is likely at any time to become a public charge, DHS will consider the statutory minimum factors and all other information relevant to assessing an applicant's likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge in the totality of the circumstances, including any receipt of means-tested public benefits, consistent with governing precedent. 90 FR 52168, 52188 (Nov. 19, 2025). INA secs. 212(a)(4)(B) and 212(s), 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(B) and 1182(s).
如本文件其他评论回复中所述,公共负担不可准入性的认定系基于个案情况,针对具体事实逐案作出,重点针对申请签证、入境许可或身份调整的外国人本人,而非其家庭成员。国土安全部指出,如果记录中有证据表明,外国人在法律上负有赡养义务的家庭成员(包括子女)因该外国人收入低于某一门槛而申请、被批准或核准领取,或正在领取或已经领取经济状况调查型公共福利,则国土安全部将在考虑范围内纳入此类家庭成员领取福利的情形。[169]在此类情况下,国土安全部将把导致该外国人家庭成员需要申请或领取此类福利的外国人自身财务状况,作为国土安全部在综合考虑全部情况时评估该外国人资产、资源和财务状况的一部分予以考量。[170]
As discussed in other comment responses, a public charge inadmissibility determination is made on an individualized, fact-specific, and case-by-case basis, focused on the alien applying for a visa, admission, or adjustment of status, not his or her family members. DHS notes that it will consider receipt of these benefits by family members, including children, to the extent there is evidence in the record that an alien's family member whom the alien is legally obligated to support applied for, was approved or certified to receive, or has received or is currently receiving means-tested public benefits due to the alien's income falling below a certain threshold.[169] In such cases, DHS would consider the alien's financial status that led to his or her family member needing to apply for or receive those benefits as part of DHS' consideration of the alien's assets, resources, and financial status in the totality of the circumstances.[170]
评论意见:多位评论者表示,取消补充营养援助计划(SNAP)注册将对移民儿童造成伤害,并引用研究表明,参与SNAP可使儿童食品不安全状况减少三分之一,而在儿童生命最初5年获得SNAP援助与终身教育成就、收入和预期寿命的改善相关联。多位评论者引用研究表明,参与SNAP的移民儿童更有可能身体健康、食品有保障并居住在稳定住房中。评论者对食品和营养福利回避将对儿童产生的影响表示担忧,包括饥饿/营养不良发生率上升、对长期健康结果的损害、儿童肥胖率上升、对长期发育的损害(包括教育成就受损),以及由于父母不得不承担额外工作以经济弥补食品援助损失而导致无人照看儿童数量增加。多位评论者指出,儿童营养减少与注意力下降、知识保持能力下降、学校参与度下降相关联,另有评论者提及营养不良如何影响情绪调节。评论者援引了过去政策变化的影响,指出在《1996年个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)通过后,身份混合家庭中超过一半的美国公民儿童退出了SNAP福利,而在2019年最终规则出台后,居住在身份混合家庭中的美国公民儿童的SNAP注册率下降了37%。
Comment: Several commenters said SNAP disenrollment would harm immigrant children, citing research showing SNAP participation reduces food insecurity in children by one third and access to SNAP for the first 5 years of a child's life is associated with improvements in lifelong educational attainment, income, and life expectancy. Several commenters referenced studies showing immigrant children who participate in SNAP are more likely to be in good health, food secure, and reside in stable housing. Commenters expressed concern about the effects that food and nutrition benefit avoidance would have on children, including increased rates of hunger/malnutrition, harm to long-term health outcomes, increased childhood obesity, harm to long-term development, including educational attainment; and increased number of children left unattended due to parents having to take on additional work to financially compensate for the loss of food aid. Several commenters remarked that reduced childhood nutrition is associated with lower concentration, ability to retain knowledge, participation in school, while another mentioned how malnutrition affects emotional regulation. Commenters cited the effects of past policy changes, noting that following the passage of the PRWORA, more than half of U.S. citizen children in mixed-status households dropped SNAP benefits and, following the 2019 Final Rule, SNAP enrollment for U.S. citizen children living in mixed status households dropped 37 percent.
回应:本规则恢复了评估与判断外国人在任何时候成为公共负担可能性相关的所有事实和情况时的广泛裁量权,并与长期以来的政策保持一致,即在美国境内的外国人应自力更生,公共福利的可获得性不应成为移民的激励因素。见8 U.S.C. 1601。本规则并不阻止任何符合健康或营养计划资格的个人申请或领取此类福利,而是忠实执行有关外国人因可能在任何时候成为公共负担而不可准入的法律规定,这正是国会在《个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)以及移民与国籍法(INA)第212(a)(4)条、8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)中所意图的。国土安全部正在落实PRWORA中国会关于外国人不应依赖公共资源满足自身需求的指示。
Response: This rule restores broad discretion to evaluate all facts and circumstances relevant to assessing an alien's likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge and align with long-standing policy that aliens in the United States should be self-reliant and that the availability of public benefits should not incentivize immigration. 8 U.S.C. 1601. This rule does not prevent any individual who is eligible for health or nutrition programs from applying for or receiving these benefits, but rather faithfully implements the statute regarding the inadmissibility of aliens who are likely at any time to become a public charge, as Congress intended in PRWORA, as well as in section 212(a)(4) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4). DHS is implementing the congressional directive in PRWORA that aliens not depend on public resources to meet their needs.
评论意见:评论者表示担忧,移民家庭中的婴儿将失去目前由妇女、婴儿和儿童特别补充营养计划(WIC)覆盖的特殊配方奶粉,这可能导致严重营养不良甚至死亡,尤其是对已经面临健康问题的婴儿而言。
Comment: Commenters expressed concern that infants in immigrant households would lose access to specialized formulas currently covered by WIC potentially causing severe malnutrition and even death, particularly for infants already facing health problems.
多位评论者表示担忧,拟议规则将导致学校膳食计划使用率下降,其中一位引用了城市研究所(Urban Institute)的一项研究,该研究显示13%的移民家庭报告因担心危及其移民身份而回避免费和减价学校膳食计划。评论者指出,学校膳食计划参与度下降将损害移民儿童的发育和整体健康。
Several commenters expressed concerns the proposed rule would lead to decreased utilization of school meal programs, with one referencing a study from the Urban Institute wherein 13 percent of immigrant families reported avoiding free and reduced school meals programs out of fear of jeopardizing their immigration status. Commenters remarked that decreased school meal participation would compromise immigrant children's development and overall health.
评论者对回避医疗保健和医疗覆盖将如何具体影响生活在身份混合家庭中的美国公民子女表示关切。一些评论者写道,2019年公共负担规则扩大后,有移民父母的儿童的医疗补助(Medicaid)和儿童健康保险计划(CHIP)参保率下降速度是其他儿童的两倍多。援引一项凯泽家庭基金会(KFF)研究,[171]一些评论者表示,美国公民子女退出医疗补助和儿童健康保险计划的人数可能远高于拟议规则的预测,放弃参保的人数估计在60万至180万之间。
Commenters expressed concerns regarding how avoidance of health care and coverage would specifically impact U.S. citizen children living in mixed-status households. A few commenters wrote that when the public charge rule was expanded in 2019, Medicaid and CHIP enrollment fell over twice as fast for children with an immigrant parent than it did for other children. Citing a KFF study,[171] a few commenters said that Medicaid and CHIP disenrollment for U.S. citizen children could be much higher than the proposed rule projects, ranging from 600,000 to 1.8 million cases of foregone enrollment.
回应:公共负担不可入境性认定专门针对申请入境或身份调整的外国人,以及该外国人在任何时候成为公共负担的可能性。因此,国土安全部(DHS)官员在作出公共负担不可入境性认定时,不会考虑外国人家庭成员领取经济状况调查类公共福利的情况。但是,正如之前的评论回应中所讨论的,由于国土安全部会考虑外国人的资产、资源和财务状况,因此在记录中有证据表明,外国人在法律上负有扶养义务的家庭成员因该外国人收入低于某一门槛而申请、获批或正在领取经济状况调查类公共福利的情况下,国土安全部会将导致其家庭成员需要申请或领取此类福利的该外国人的财务状况,作为整体情况考量中该外国人资产、资源和财务状况的一部分予以考虑。美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)的次级法规指南将明确,审理身份调整申请的官员仅应按上述方式考虑外国人领取经济状况调查类公共福利的情况。
Response: The public charge inadmissibility determination is squarely focused on aliens applying for admission or adjustment of status and the likelihood such an alien will at any time become a public charge. Therefore, DHS officers will not consider the receipt of means-tested public benefits by the alien's household members when making a public charge inadmissibility determination. However, as discussed in previous comment responses, because DHS considers the alien's assets, resources, and financial status, to the extent that there is evidence in the record that an alien's family member whom the alien is legally obligated to support applied for, was approved or certified to receive, or has received or is currently receiving means-tested public benefits due to the alien's income falling below a certain threshold, DHS will consider the alien's financial status that lead to his or her family member needing to apply for or receive those benefits as part the alien's assets, resources, and financial status in the totality of the circumstances. USCIS subregulatory guidance will clarify that officers who adjudicate adjustment of status applications should only consider the receipt of means-tested public benefits by the alien as outlined above.
国土安全部认识到本最终规则可能对公共卫生产生间接影响。然而,本政策的收益超过了本规则的成本,因为它确保国土安全部忠实地适用(第45367页)公共负担不可入境性条款,其方式符合国会的意图,即外国人应自给自足,依靠自身能力以及其家庭、担保人和私人组织的资源,而不是依赖公共资源。见《美国法典》第8编第1601条。
DHS recognizes this final rule may have indirect impacts on public health. However, the benefits of this policy outweigh the costs of this rule by ensuring that DHS faithfully applies the ( printed page 45367) public charge ground of inadmissibility in a manner that is consistent with Congress's intent that aliens are self-sufficient and are relying on their own capabilities and resources of their family, sponsor, and private organizations, rather than depending on public resources. 8 U.S.C. 1601.
d. 对孕妇的影响
d. Impact on Pregnant Women
评论:许多评论者对寒蝉效应对孕妇的影响表示关切,称在拟议修改下,孕妇和产后母亲可能不太愿意申领福利,从而导致不良的分娩结果。评论者表示,为移民孕妇群体扩大医疗补助覆盖范围可增加产前护理的使用,进而改善分娩结果。他们指出,退出公共福利项目与孕妇或哺乳期妇女营养不良和肥胖发生率上升存在关联。
Comment: Many commenters expressed concern about the impact of chilling effects on pregnant women, stating pregnant and post-partum mothers may be less likely to claim benefits under the proposed changes, leading to adverse birth outcomes. Commenters said that expanded Medicaid coverage for pregnant immigrant populations increases the use of prenatal care and, in turn, improves birth outcomes. They stated that disenrollment from public benefits programs is associated with increased prevalence of malnutrition and obesity among pregnant or breastfeeding women.
许多评论者强调了公共政策方面的关切,并表示该规则将导致获得产前项目的机会减少,从而使婴儿和孕产妇健康状况恶化,并提高孕产妇和婴儿死亡率。一位评论者援引了有妇女因担心危及其移民身份而退还吸奶器的报道。评论者表示,妇女、婴儿和儿童特别营养补充项目(WIC)为低收入社区提供了重要服务,包括食品援助、母乳喂养支持以及改善产前护理的获取机会,并且WIC的参与可将婴儿死亡率降低三分之一。
Many commenters highlighted public policy concerns and stated that the rule would result in decreased access to prenatal programs, leading to worsened infant and maternal health outcomes and higher maternal and infant mortality rates. One commenter cited reports of women returning breast pumps out of fear of jeopardizing their immigration status. Commenters said that WIC offers vital services for low-income communities, including food assistance, support with breastfeeding, and improved access to prenatal care, and that WIC participation reduces infant mortality by one third.
评论者讨论了因退出健康保险而导致产前护理机会减少所带来的负面健康后果,包括妊娠糖尿病发病率上升、肾脏感染增加、血压升高、分娩结果恶化、早产数量增加、出生体重降低、新生儿低血糖症例增加、婴儿神经发育障碍发生率上升,以及新生儿贫血病例增加。一位评论者预计,由于医疗补助(Medicaid)退出和产前护理机会减少所导致的急诊室使用率上升、传染病增加以及代价高昂的疾病和伤害,各州预算将需要增加支出来应对,此外还需增加支出以提供婴儿配方奶粉。评论者援引多项研究指出,在2017年公共负担规则最初泄露之后,移民妇女的产前医疗补助参保率出现大幅下降,导致移民新生儿的出生体重下降。
Commenters discussed the negative health outcomes that disenrollment from health insurance and, in turn, decreased access to prenatal care results in upticks in gestational diabetes, increased kidney infections, higher blood pressure, worsened birth outcomes, increased number of preterm births, lowered birth weights, increased instances of hypoglycemia at birth, increased rates of infant neurodevelopmental disorders, and increased cases of anemia in newborns. One commenter anticipated additional spending in State budgets to address higher rates of emergency room use, increased infectious diseases, and costly illness and injury caused by Medicaid disenrollment and decreased access to prenatal care, as well as additional spending to provide formula. Referencing multiple studies, commenters wrote that, following the initial leak of the public charge rule in 2017, Medicaid saw significant drops in prenatal Medicaid enrollment from immigrant women, resulting in drops in birth weights among newborn immigrant babies.
少数评论者表示担忧,在拟议规则下,移民妇女将回避避孕服务。评论者指出,获得避孕服务对妇女的健康结果至关重要,并补充说,美国移民妇女目前已经比美国出生的妇女更不可能获得性与生殖健康服务的保障并加以使用。
A few commenters expressed concern that under the proposed rule, immigrant women would avoid contraceptive services. Commenters remarked that access to contraception is critical for women's health outcomes, adding that immigrant women in the United States are already less likely to have coverage for and use sexual and reproductive health services than U.S.-born women.
回应:国土安全部(DHS)同意,产前护理,包括通过医疗补助(Medicaid)以及其他经济状况审查类医疗项目提供的产前护理,为接受护理的孕妇(及其妊娠中的胎儿)提供了重要益处,并对个人和公共健康均有积极影响。然而,国会指示国土安全部根据《1996年个人责任与工作机会协调法案》(PRWORA)的规定,最大限度地减少外国人因公共福利的可获得性而企图移民或在美国调整身份的动机,并促进在美国境内的外国人实现自给自足。参见8 U.S.C. 1601。正如在其他评论回应中所讨论的,本规则既未改变经济状况审查类公共福利的资格要求,也未阻止个人申请或获得其有资格享有的任何经济状况审查类公共福利。尽管国土安全部认识到本最终规则可能对孕妇产生间接影响,但国土安全部认为,该政策的益处超过了对某些人群的此类间接影响,因为本规则符合国会意图,确保因公共负担不可入境事由而受审查的申请入境或调整身份的外国人,如果未能证明其依靠自身能力和资源,或其家庭、担保人及私人组织的资源,而非依赖公共资源来满足其需求,则将被拒绝。国土安全部不同意孕妇接受经济状况审查类公共福利不应在公共负担认定中予以考虑的观点。与儿童类似,国会并未将孕妇排除在公共负担不可入境事由之外,国土安全部必须适用该事由,除非该外国人是以豁免类别申请入境或调整身份。
Response: DHS agrees prenatal care, including through Medicaid as well as other means-tested healthcare programs, provides important benefits to expectant mothers (and gestating children) who receive it and has positive impacts on both individual and public health. However, Congress instructed DHS to minimize the incentive for aliens who attempt to immigrate or adjust status in the United States due to the availability of public benefits and promote the self-sufficiency of aliens within the United States, in accordance with PRWORA. See8 U.S.C. 1601. As discussed in other comment responses, this rule neither changes the eligibility requirements for means-tested public benefits nor precludes individuals from applying for or receiving any means-tested public benefit for which they are eligible. While DHS recognizes that this final rule may have indirect impacts on pregnant women, DHS believes that the benefits of this policy outweigh any such indirect impacts on certain populations because this rule, consistent with congressional intent, ensures that aliens applying for admission or adjustment of status who are subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility, are denied if they fail to demonstrate that they are relying on their own capabilities and resources of their family, sponsor, and private organizations, rather than depending on public resources to meet their needs. DHS does not agree receipt of means-tested public benefits by pregnant women should not be considered in a public charge determination. Similar to children, Congress did not exclude pregnant women from the public charge ground of inadmissibility and DHS must apply the ground unless the alien is seeking admission or adjustment of status in an exempt classification.
因此,在确定外国人是否属于不可入境之列时,国土安全部将考虑该外国人是否接受了提供产前护理的任何经济状况审查类公共福利,包括通过医疗补助(Medicaid)以及其他为孕妇和妊娠中胎儿提供服务的经济状况审查类医疗项目,如本规则通篇所述。[172]然而,国土安全部在综合考量情况时,将考虑到这些福利与一种暂时性状况,即妊娠,相关这一事实。国土安全部还将考虑接受这些福利的数额和时间的近期程度,包括参与该项目是否属于孤立情形,以及与外国人具体情况相关的所有其他信息,并在综合考量中纳入法定最低限度因素。
Therefore, when determining whether an alien is inadmissible, DHS will consider the alien's receipt of any means-tested public benefits that provide prenatal care, including through Medicaid, as well as other means-tested healthcare programs for expectant mothers and gestating children as outlined throughout this rule.[172] However, DHS will consider the fact that these benefits are related to a temporary condition—pregnancy—when considering the alien's receipt in the totality of the circumstances. DHS will also consider amount and recency of receipt of these benefits, including whether participation in the program was isolated, along with all other information relevant to the aliens' specific circumstances in the totality of the circumstances, including the statutory minimum factors.
在评论者暗示本最终规则将导致妇女因对其外籍家庭成员移民福利申请的影响而无法获得与其健康有关的某些福利的范围内,国土安全部(DHS)指出,只有在记录中有证据表明外国人在法律上有义务扶养的家庭成员因该外国人的收入低于某一门槛而申请、被批准或核准领取、或已经领取或正在领取经济状况调查类公共福利的情况下,国土安全部才会考虑家庭成员领取这些福利的情况。正如此前评论回应中所讨论的,国土安全部将在对外国人的资产、资源和财务状况进行整体情况考量时,把导致其家庭成员需要申请或领取这些福利的外国人的财务状况纳入考虑范围。[173]
To the extent that these commenters suggest this final rule will result in women not accessing certain benefits related to their health due to the impact on their alien family members' applications for immigration benefits, DHS notes that it will only consider receipt of these benefits by family members to the extent that there is evidence in the record that an alien's family member whom the alien is legally obligated to support applied for, was approved or certified to receive, or has received or is currently receiving means-tested public benefits due to the alien's income falling below a certain threshold. As discussed in previous comment responses, DHS will consider the alien's financial status that led to his or her family member needing to apply for or receive those benefits as part of DHS' consideration of the alien's assets, resources, and financial status in the totality of the circumstances.[173]
e. 对残疾人士的影响
e. Impact on People With Disabilities
评论意见:评论者对本规则对患有残疾或慢性病的家庭成员的照顾者所产生的影响表示关切,指出该规则会给为家庭成员申请残疾福利的移民造成不必要的恐惧,即使这些家庭成员是美国公民也是如此。一位评论者指出,患有残疾儿童的父母,即使拥有医疗保险且收入属于中产阶层,也可能由于诸如居家支持服务(In-Home(印刷页45368)Supportive Services)和独立生活服务(Independent Living Services)等服务的高昂费用,而不得不依赖公共福利来满足患有残疾的子女在医疗、教育和治疗支持方面的健康与福祉需求。其他评论者表示,一些照顾者必须离开劳动力市场以照顾其家庭成员,这些家庭不应该因此还要放弃必要的残疾服务。评论者提出,由于该规则所带来的额外压力,可能导致照顾者出现倦怠。其中一位评论者表示,当残疾家庭成员失去所需服务的获取渠道,或因恐惧而退出相关项目时,负担就会转移到通常是父母、配偶或大家庭成员的无偿照顾者身上。该评论者强调了该规则对特定群体的影响,并补充说照顾者中有色人种妇女所占比例过高,将受到最大影响。
Comment: Commenters expressed concern about the effects of the rule on caregivers of family members with a disability or chronic condition, citing the unnecessary fear the rule would create for immigrants applying for disability benefits for family members, even when those family members are U.S. citizens. One commenter pointed out that parents of children with disabilities, even those with medical insurance who earn middle class incomes, may rely on public benefits for medical, educational, and therapeutic supports for health and wellbeing for children with a disability due to the high cost of services such as In-Home ( printed page 45368) Supportive Services and Independent Living Services. Others said some caregivers must leave the workforce to care for their family member and that these families should not have to also decline necessary disability services. Commenters raised possible caregiver burnout due to the additional stresses resulting from the rule. One of these commenters said that when disabled family members lose access to services they need, or withdraw from programs out of fear, the burden shifts to unpaid caregivers who are often parents, spouses, or extended family members. The commenter emphasized the impact on specific communities, adding caregivers are disproportionately women of color and would be most affected.
一位评论者指出,该规则缺乏明确性,也没有针对患有残疾或慢性病的人士所领取福利设立例外规定,这将迫使家庭在因移民后果而维持家庭团聚与获取重要服务之间做出选择。另一位评论者表示,该规则将导致个人护理以及居家与社区服务的获取减少,而这些服务对残疾人士及整个家庭系统的福祉而言是必不可少的。
One commenter identified the lack of clarity in the rule or exceptions for benefits received by individuals with a disability or chronic condition would force families to choose between staying together and accessing vital services due to immigration consequences. Another said the rule would result in reduced access to personal care and home and community-based services, which is essential for individuals with a disability and the well-being of entire family systems.
回应:本规则使国土安全部恢复忠实适用有关公共负担不可入境性认定的法规及国会立法意图,并不会阻止个人申请或获得其有资格享有的福利。国土安全部不同意本规则会阻止美国公民获得其有资格享有的福利这一观点。正如其他评论回应中所讨论的,国土安全部承认,受本规则约束的外国人可能会为避免本最终规则所带来的负面后果,而选择不为其子女登记注册其子女依据《1996年个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)有资格享有的经济状况调查类公共福利,或选择为其子女办理退出登记。国土安全部只有在记录中有证据表明外国人在法律上有义务扶养的家庭成员因该外国人的收入低于某一门槛而申请、被批准或核准领取、或已经领取或正在领取经济状况调查类公共福利的情况下,才会考虑作为外国人家庭一部分的美国公民领取经济状况调查类公共福利的情况。在此类情况下,国土安全部将在对外国人的资产、资源和财务状况进行整体情况考量时,把导致其家庭成员需要申请或领取这些福利的外国人的财务状况纳入考虑范围。[174]
Response: This rule returns DHS to faithfully applying the statute and intent of Congress regarding public charge inadmissibility determinations and does not prevent individuals from applying for or obtaining benefits for which they are eligible. DHS disagrees this rule prevents U.S. citizens from obtaining benefits for which they are eligible. As discussed in other comment responses, DHS acknowledges aliens subject to this rule may decline to enroll their children in, or may choose to disenroll their children from, means-tested public benefits for which their children are eligible under PRWORA, in order to avoid negative consequences as a result of this final rule. DHS will only take into consideration the receipt of means-tested public benefits by U.S. citizens who are part of the alien's household to the extent that there is evidence in the record that an alien's family member whom the alien is legally obligated to support applied for, was approved or certified to receive, or has received or is currently receiving means-tested public benefits due to the alien's income falling below a certain threshold. In such cases, DHS would consider the alien's financial status that led to his or her family member needing to apply for or receive those benefits as part of DHS' consideration of the alien's assets, resources, and financial status in the totality of the circumstances.[174]
国土安全部(DHS)认为,美国公民和获得公共负担不可准入性豁免的外国人,如果因本规则而退出公共福利计划或放弃参加该计划,是没有必要的,因为此类人员并不受本规则约束。国土安全部有责任忠实执行相关规定以及公共负担不可准入性依据,其方式须符合国会的意图,即外国人应自给自足,依靠自身能力以及其家人、担保人和私人组织的资源。见《美国法典》第8编第1601(2)(A)条。根据《康复法》第504条,国土安全部被禁止仅因残疾而在接受联邦财政资助的任何项目或活动中,或在任何由联邦实施的项目或活动中,歧视合格的残疾人士。如拟议规则制定通知(NPRM)中所述,在涉及任何残疾的情形下,官员将遵守现行法律,并考虑外国人的残疾在何种程度上可能影响其自给自足的能力,以确保残疾不会成为判断外国人在任何时候成为公共负担可能性的唯一决定因素。见2025年11月19日《联邦公报》第90卷第52168页、第52188页。
DHS believes it would be unwarranted for U.S. citizens and aliens exempt from public charge inadmissibility to disenroll from a public benefit program or forgo enrollment in response to this rule when such individuals are not subject to this rule. DHS is responsible for faithfully applying the and the public charge ground of inadmissibility in a manner consistent with Congress's intent that aliens are self-sufficient and rely on their own capabilities and the resources of their families, their sponsors, and private organizations. 8 U.S.C. 1601(2)(A). DHS is prohibited under section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act from discrimination against a qualified individual with a disability solely on the basis of that disability under any program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance or under any federally conducted program or activity. As noted in the NPRM, in the context of any disability, officers will comply with existing law and consider whether or to what extent an alien's disability is likely to impact his or her ability to be self-sufficient, ensuring that disability is not used as the sole determinant of an alien's likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge. See90 FR 52168, 52188 (Nov. 19, 2025).
国土安全部对评论者关于获得居家和社区服务机会的关切表示理解。国土安全部指出,在审议外国人申请、获批或获认证接受,或当前和/或过去接受任何经济状况审查类公共福利的情况时,国土安全部会综合考虑该福利的性质以及接受福利的周边情况,例如接受的时间近期程度、持续时间、接受数额、接受原因,以及该原因是否可能持续存在。在考虑接受旨在以远低于长期机构护理成本的方式满足受益人需求的居家和社区服务时,[175]国土安全部同时也会考虑到,在综合考量各种情况后,此类服务的成本更为低廉这一事实。
DHS appreciates the commenters' concern about access to home and community-based services. DHS notes that in considering an alien's application for, approval or certification for receipt, or current and/or past receipt of any means-tested public benefits, DHS considers the nature of the benefit along with the surrounding circumstances for receipt, such as the recency, duration, amount of receipt, reason for receipt, and whether the reason has likelihood to persist. When considering the receipt of home and community-based services intended to meet the needs of beneficiaries at a fraction of the cost of long-term institutional care,[175] DHS also considers the fact that such services are less costly in the totality of the circumstances.
然而,国土安全部重申,本规则旨在遵循《个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)的指示,即外国人应自给自足,不应依赖公共资源,因此,国土安全部拒绝为避免受本规则约束的个人可能退出或选择不参加经济状况审查类公共福利计划的可能性,而限制本规则制定的效力。国土安全部将以个案方式作出公共负担不可准入性的认定,如果外国人曾申请、已获批准或认证接受,或已经接受或正在接受任何经济状况审查类公共福利,国土安全部无法保证该外国人不会因公共负担理由而被认定为不可准入。
DHS reiterates, however, that this rule is intended to follow PRWORA's directive that aliens should be self-sufficient and not be dependent on public resources and therefore, DHS declines to limit the effect of the rulemaking to avoid the possibility that individuals subject to this rule may disenroll or choose not to enroll in means-tested public benefits. DHS will make public charge inadmissibility determinations on an individualized basis and cannot ensure an alien will not be found inadmissible under the public charge ground if he or she applied for, has been approved or certified to receive, or has received or is currently receiving any means-tested public benefits.
国土安全部同样理解人们对本规则适用范围及效力存在困惑可能带来的影响。尽管国土安全部无法完全消除本最终规则下的公共负担不可准入性认定在实践中对某些群体造成比其他群体更为不利影响的可能性,但美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)将对官员进行培训,并就本最终规则下公共负担不可准入性认定的各个方面发布指导意见,以支持个案认定的准确性、一致性和可靠性。至于有关种族和性别差异的评论,国土安全部在本规则其他部分将更充分地论述有关偏见和歧视的关切。
DHS also appreciates the potential effects of confusion regarding the rule's scope and effect. While DHS cannot completely eliminate the possibility that public charge inadmissibility determinations under this final rule will, in practice, negatively impact some groups more than others, USCIS will provide training to officers and issue guidance on all aspects of public charge inadmissibility determinations made under this final rule, to support accuracy, consistency, and reliability in individual determinations. As to the comment regarding racial and gender disparities, DHS addresses concerns about bias and discrimination more fully elsewhere in this rule.
评论:许多评论者对本规则给依赖医疗、教育和治疗支持以维持健康与福祉的残疾儿童所带来的影响表示关切,并指出家长已经因担心移民后果而放弃这些支持。评论者表示,儿童将错失自闭症和发育迟缓的早期识别与干预窗口期。一位评论者指出,根据《残疾人教育法》,任何符合条件的残疾儿童均可获得特殊教育服务,不论其家庭收入如何。
Comment: Many commenters were concerned about the effects of the rule on children with disabilities who rely on medical, education, and therapeutic supports for their health and well-being and that parents are already declining these supports for fear of immigration consequences. Commenters stated children will miss early identification and intervention windows for autism and developmental delays. One commenter pointed out that special education services under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act are available to any child with a disability who qualifies, regardless of income.
回应:美国国土安全部(DHS)认为,根据《1996年个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA),必须最大限度减少外国人因可获得公共福利而寻求移民至美国或在美国调整身份的动机,并促进外国人在美国的自给自足能力。参见8 U.S.C. 1601。美国国土安全部承认,受本规则约束的外国人可能会拒绝登记领取或选择停止领取其根据《1996年个人责任与工作机会协调法》可能有资格获得的公共福利,以避免因本最终规则而产生的不利后果。(印刷页第45369页)然而,美国国土安全部有权在评估外国人在任何时候成为公共负担的可能性时,考虑其对经济状况调查型公共福利的申请、批准或认证领取,以及当前和/或过去的领取情况,即使此类考虑最终可能导致外国人不愿领取其有资格获得的经济状况调查型公共福利。美国国土安全部认为,如本规则通篇所述,这样做的益处超过了因父母选择拒绝可获得的支持而对子女造成的任何间接不利影响。尽管个人可能会因考虑到未来的移民后果而重新考虑是否领取经济状况调查型公共福利,但本规则并不禁止外国人获得其有资格获得的任何经济状况调查型公共福利。
Response: DHS believes it must minimize the incentive for aliens to seek to immigrate to, or adjust status in, the United States due to the availability of public benefits and promote the self-sufficiency of aliens within the United States, in accordance with PRWORA. See8 U.S.C. 1601. DHS acknowledges that aliens subject to this rule may decline to enroll in, or may choose to ( printed page 45369) disenroll from, public benefits for which they may be eligible under PRWORA, in order to avoid negative consequences as a result of this final rule. However, DHS has authority to consider applications for, approval or certification for receipt, and current and/or past receipt of means-tested public benefits when assessing an alien's likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge, even where such actions may ultimately result in discouraging aliens from receiving means-tested public benefits for which they are eligible, and DHS believes the benefits of doing so, as described throughout this rule, outweigh any negative indirect effects to children if parents choose to decline available supports. Although individuals may reconsider their receipt of means-tested public benefits in light of future immigration consequences, this rule does not prohibit an alien from obtaining any means-tested public benefit for which he or she is eligible.
为解决有关领取公共福利的担忧,正如本最终规则其他部分所述,对于那些资格并非基于外国人收入或资产、而是不论个人收入高低均可获得的福利,将不予考虑,因为这些福利并非经济状况调查型福利。
To address the concerns about receipt of public benefits whose eligibility is not based on an alien's income or assets and instead are available to every individual regardless of their income, as stated elsewhere in this final rule, those benefits would not be considered because they are not means-tested.
评论:一位评论者指出,将残疾人排除在诸如低收入家庭能源援助计划等非现金援助项目之外,将直接针对那些需要电力来支持医疗设备(如呼吸机和电动轮椅)的人群,并指出许多此类家庭中有成员患有严重疾病。
Comment: One commenter stated that the exclusion of people with disabilities from non-cash assistance programs such as Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program would directly target people who require electricity to support medical equipment, such as ventilators and power wheelchairs, pointing out that many such households include members with serious medical conditions.
回应:美国国土安全部不同意本规则直接针对因健康或医疗状况而领取非现金福利的个人这一说法。美国国土安全部认定,考虑外国人对经济状况调查型公共福利的申请、批准或认证领取,以及任何当前或过去的领取情况,符合国会的意图,即身在美国境内的外国人应自给自足,并依靠自身能力以及其家庭、担保人和私人组织的资源。参见8 U.S.C. 1601。如前所述,在考虑外国人对经济状况调查型公共福利的申请、批准或认证领取,或任何当前或过去的领取情况时,美国国土安全部将考虑该福利的性质以及领取时的具体情况,例如领取的时间近远、持续时间、领取金额、领取原因,以及该原因是否可能持续存在。然而,本规则并无任何条款指示外国人停止领取任何经济状况调查型公共福利。
Response: DHS disagrees the rule directly targets individuals who receive non-cash benefits related to their health or medical conditions. DHS determined considering applications for, approval or certification for receipt, or any current or past receipt of means-tested public benefits is consistent with Congress's intent that aliens inside the United States are self-sufficient and rely on their own capabilities and the resources of their families, sponsors, and private organizations. See8 U.S.C. 1601. As discussed previously, when considering an alien's applications for, approval or certification for receipt, or any current or past receipt of means-tested public benefits, DHS will consider the nature of the benefit as well as the circumstances surrounding receipt, such as the recency, duration, amount of receipt, reason for receipt, and whether the reason has likelihood to persist. However, nothing in this rule directs aliens to disenroll from any means-tested public benefit.
评论:一个组织评论称,鉴于长期存在的机构化偏见,不应将接受机构照护视为潜在的不利因素,并表示担忧本规则将增加残疾人士或患有慢性病的个人住院或被安置于机构的风险。
Comment: One organization commented that institutionalization should not be considered as a potential negative factor given longstanding institutional bias and expressed concern that the rule would increase the risk of hospitalization or institutional placement for individuals with a disability or chronic condition.
该组织补充说,医疗补助计划(Medicaid)和残疾服务体系历来使机构照护比居家及社区服务更易获得、资金更为稳定,因此被安置于机构往往是由于体系限制,而非个人选择或需求所致。对移民后果的担忧可能导致个人回避社区服务,并增加可预防的健康支持缺口升级为危机、最终导致机构安置的可能性,这将损害个人的自主性、安全性和生活质量。他们指出,如果个人因担忧而回避或无法利用社区支持服务,将导致各州承担更高的成本。
This organization added that Medicaid and disability service systems have historically made institutional care easier to access and more consistently funded than home- and community-based services, so placement in institutions is often driven by system constraints rather than individual choice or need. Fear of immigration consequences may result in individuals avoiding community-based services and increases in the likelihood that preventable health supports or gaps escalate into crises that result in institutional placement, and undermines autonomy, safety, and quality of life. They pointed out that institutionalization would result in higher costs for States if individuals avoid or are not able to take advantage of community-based supports due to fear.
答复:国土安全部(DHS)承认,当患者失去医疗保障时,州或地方政府承担的总体成本可能会增加,并且可能对患者及其家庭和社区产生长期影响。然而,国土安全部已确定,与其他经济状况调查类公共福利一样,由政府出资进行长期机构化护理表明该外国人缺乏自给自足能力,且依赖政府满足其需求。国土安全部没有数据可用于评估有多少外国人既属于公共负担不予许可事由的适用对象,又由政府出资接受长期机构化护理(包括此类服务由医疗补助计划(Medicaid)承保的情形),因此无法量化在最终规则中保留这一长期政策的影响。然而,国土安全部认为该影响很小。国土安全部指出,在考虑外国人领取经济状况调查类公共福利的情况时,国土安全部会一并考虑该福利的性质以及外国人领取该福利的相关情况,例如领取的近期程度、持续时间、领取金额、领取原因,以及该原因是否可能持续存在。
Response: DHS acknowledges that when patients lose medical coverage, overall costs to State or local governments may increase, and there may be long-term consequences for patients and their families and communities. However, DHS has determined that, like other means-tested public benefits, long-term institutionalization at government expense is indicative of an alien's lack of self-sufficiency and dependence on the government to meet his or her needs. DHS does not have data to assess how many aliens are both subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility and are institutionalized on a long-term basis at government expense, including when such services are covered by Medicaid, and as a result, is unable to quantify the impact of retaining this long-standing policy in the final rule. However, DHS believes the impact is small. DHS notes that in considering an alien's receipt of means-tested public benefits, DHS considers the nature of the benefit along with the circumstances surrounding the alien's receipt, such as the recency, duration, amount of receipt, reason for receipt, and whether the reason has likelihood to persist.
关于居家和社区服务的评论,国土安全部承认,这些服务能够以长期机构护理成本的一小部分满足受益人的需求。[176]在考虑领取居家和社区服务的情况时,国土安全部会考虑这些福利的目的,以及这些福利相较于长期机构化护理成本更低这一事实。然而,国土安全部重申,国会的意图始终是要求外国人自给自足,国土安全部为忠实适用法律,不基于此项评论对规则作出修改。
As to the comments about home and community-based services, DHS acknowledges that these services meet the needs of beneficiaries at a fraction of the cost of long-term institutional care.[176] When considering the receipt of home and community-based services, DHS considers the purpose of these benefits as well as the fact that these benefits are less costly than long-term institutionalization. However, DHS reiterates that Congress's intent has consistently been that aliens are self-sufficient, and DHS declines to make changes to the rule based on this comment in order to faithfully apply the law.
六、对暴力和人口贩运幸存者的影响
f. Impact on Survivors of Violence and Trafficking
评论:有评论者指出,该规则将危及暴力行为幸存者的安全与稳定,导致幸存者因担心移民后果而退出庇护所和危机援助项目或寻求其他帮助,并增加暴力幸存者为经济保障而返回施暴者身边的风险。一位评论者强调,即使是美国公民幸存者,如果其家庭成员将来可能寻求入境许可或其他移民福利,也可能因此而不敢寻求帮助。
Comment: Commenters stated the rule would risk the safety and stability of survivors of violence, causing survivors to withdraw from shelters and crisis programs or seek other help due to fear of immigration consequences and increasing the risk of survivors of violence returning to their abusers for financial security. One commenter emphasized even U.S. citizen survivors may be afraid of seeking assistance if they have a family member who may seek admission or another immigration benefit in the future.
多位评论者指出,该规则强化了施暴者用以孤立和控制暴力幸存者的结构性条件,助长了这些施暴者的气焰,同时将幸存者困于危险境地,使其生命安全受到威胁,并阻碍其举报犯罪或寻求帮助。两位评论者举例说明,该规则将允许国土安全部以一名家庭暴力幸存者曾向警方举报施暴者并通过当地警察局获得受害人服务以保障自身及其子女安全为由,拒绝授予其合法永久居民身份。
Several commenters stated the rule reinforces structural conditions abusers use to isolate and control survivors of violence, and empowers those abusers while trapping survivors in dangerous situations, putting their lives at risk, and deterring them from reporting crimes or seeking help. Two commenters provided the example that the rule would permit DHS to deny LPR status to a survivor of domestic violence because she reported her abuser to the police and received victim services through the local police department to ensure her safety and that of her children.
答复:国土安全部坚决不同意该规则会危及暴力幸存者的安全与稳定、强化有利于施暴者的结构性条件或助长施暴者气焰的说法。根据国会在《移民与国籍法》(INA)第212(a)(4)条(即8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4))项下的规定,任何申请进入美国的外国人,如在任何时候有可能成为公共负担,均不予许可入境。根据《针对妇女的暴力行为法》(VAWA)[177]以自我申请方式调整身份的家庭暴力幸存者,(第45370页)不适用公共负担不予许可事由。因此,在裁决其身份调整申请时,不会考虑其领取任何经济状况调查类公共福利或其他受害人服务的情况。根据适用公共负担不予许可事由的类别调整身份的家庭暴力幸存者,依据本规则并不被禁止领取经济状况调查类公共福利或其他服务。但是,国土安全部将在综合考量该外国人整体情况时,考虑其领取任何经济状况调查类公共福利的情况,以及记录中显示该外国人曾申请或已获批准或认定可领取任何经济状况调查类公共福利的任何证据,包括该福利的性质、领取的近期程度、持续时间和金额、领取原因,以及该原因是否已经或可能持续存在。《联邦公报》第90卷第52168页,第52188页(2025年11月19日)。
Response: DHS strongly disagrees that the rule risks safety and stability of survivors of violence, reinforces structural conditions that benefit abusers, or empowers abusers. As mandated by Congress under section 212(a)(4) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4), any alien applying for admission to the United States is inadmissible if he or she is likely at any time to become a public charge. Survivors of domestic violence adjusting status as self- ( printed page 45370) petitioners under VAWA [177] are exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility. Therefore, any receipt of means-tested public benefits or other victim services will not be considered when adjudicating their application for adjustment of status. Survivors of domestic violence adjusting status under a category that is subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility are not prevented from receiving means-tested public benefits or other services under this rule. But, DHS will consider receipt of any means-tested public benefits, as well as any evidence in the record that the alien applied for or has been approved or certified to receive any means-tested public benefits, in the totality of alien's circumstances, including the nature of the benefit, the recency, duration, and amount of receipt, the reason for the receipt, and whether the reason has or is likely to persist. 90 FR 52168, 52188 (Nov. 19, 2025).
评论:一位评论者表示,该规则阻碍寻求U类和T类非移民签证的受害者寻求帮助,并破坏了相关法规的立法目的,存在被依据《行政程序法》(APA)及既定的制定法解释原则宣布为非法的风险,并敦促国土安全部(DHS)保留对暴力和贩运受害者的保护。另一位评论者以类似理由要求国土安全部撤回该规则。
Comment: A commenter said the rule deters survivors seeking U and T nonimmigrant visas from seeking help and undermines the purpose of the statutes, risks being declared unlawful under the APA and established principles of statutory interpretation, and urged DHS to preserve protections for survivors of violence and trafficking. Another commenter requested DHS withdraw the rule for similar reasons.
回应:国土安全部强烈不同意该最终规则会阻碍犯罪或贩运受害者寻求帮助或破坏该法规立法目的的说法。寻求T类和U类非移民身份的外国人可免于适用公共负担不可入境事由。同样,已提交T类或U类非移民身份表面成立(prima facie)申请的外国人,或已获得T类或U类非移民身份且正依据《移民与国籍法》(INA)第245(a)、(l)或(m)条,即8 U.S.C. 1255(a)、(l)或(m)条申请调整身份的外国人,也同样可免于适用公共负担不可入境事由。[178]最后,根据《1996年个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)被认定为“合格外国人”的某些受虐外国人,同样可免于适用公共负担不可入境事由。[179]由于这些外国人不受公共负担不可入境事由的约束,在审理其身份调整申请时,将不考虑其领取经济状况审查类公共福利的情况。
Response: DHS strongly disagrees that the Final Rule deters survivors of crime or trafficking from seeking help or undermines the statute. Aliens seeking T and U nonimmigrant status are exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility. Similarly, aliens with prima facie applications for T or U nonimmigrant status, or who were granted T or U nonimmigrant status who are applying to adjust status under sections 245(a), (l), or (m) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1255(a), (l), or (m), are exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility.[178] Finally, certain battered aliens who are “qualified aliens” under PRWORA are similarly exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility.[179] Because these aliens are not subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility, their receipt of means-tested public benefits will not be considered when adjudicating their applications for adjustment.
七、对托儿服务工作人员的影响
g. Impact on Child Care Workers
评论:多位评论者对拟议规则可能给托儿服务工作人员带来的影响表示担忧。鉴于托儿服务工作人员中有22%为移民,一位评论者指出,拟议规则中的模糊之处将使从事幼儿教育工作的移民工作者望而却步而不敢领取公共福利,其中一些人因工资低而依赖公共福利,这将加剧人员短缺问题,并特别指出,部分原因在于美国移民及海关执法局(ICE)近期的拘捕行动,自2025年1月以来,托儿服务行业中的移民女性工作者减少了39,000人,有学龄前儿童的美国母亲参与劳动力市场的人数减少了77,000人。
Comment: Commenters voiced concern about the proposed rule's potential impact on child care workers. Given 22 percent of child care workers are immigrants, one commenter suggested that ambiguity in the proposed rule would discourage early education immigrant workers, some of whom rely on public benefits due to low wages, from utilizing public benefits, exacerbating staffing shortages, noting in part due to recent U.S Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrests, since January 2025, there are 39,000 fewer immigrant women in the child care workforce and 77,000 fewer American mothers of preschool-age children in the workforce.
回应:国土安全部(DHS)不同意本最终规则含糊不清或认为废止2022年最终规则将导致托儿工作者退出劳动力市场的观点。如其他意见回应中所述,国土安全部在《立法建议预告》(NPRM)中已明确表示,并在本最终规则中再次明确,在废止2022年最终规则后,官员将能够考虑受公共负担可予拒绝入境理由约束的外国人所获得的所有经济状况审查类公共福利的领取情况。国土安全部澄清,先前被排除在外的经济状况审查类公共福利,如果是在本最终规则生效日期之前领取的,将不予考虑;而外国人家庭成员领取的经济状况审查类公共福利,仅在与外国人的资产、资源和财务状况相关的特定情形下才会被考虑。最后,托儿工作者领取经济状况审查类公共福利只是全面情况考量中的一项因素,官员仍拥有充分的自由裁量权,可以考虑与公共负担可予拒绝入境认定相关的所有其他信息和证据。国土安全部既不反驳低薪托儿工作者领取经济状况审查类公共福利的论点,也不反驳托儿工作者在劳动力市场中发挥重要作用的论点。然而,尽管本规则可能导致某些外国人放弃领取经济状况审查类公共福利,国土安全部不同意本规则将导致外国籍托儿工作者退出劳动力市场的观点;如果这些外国人继续留在美国,他们将需要继续工作以维持自己和家人的生活。此外,这些外国人应当依靠自身资源以及亲属、朋友或私人组织的资源来补充收入,而不是依赖政府项目来满足自身需求。参见8 U.S.C. 1601(2)(A)。最后,国土安全部指出,评论者所引用的有关托儿劳动力的研究虽然具有一定启示性,但并不直接支持评论者所提出的主张。具体而言,关于早期护理和教育劳动力中移民比例的研究,基于美国社区调查(ACS)数据,无法区分作为合法永久居民(LPR)的外国人(因此不受公共负担可予拒绝入境理由约束)与非合法永久居民的外国人(他们未来可能寻求调整身份或被允许入境美国,因而受本规则影响)。[180] 评论者引用的关于“43%的托儿工作者使用公共援助”这一说法的研究,其数据包括家庭或户内成员获得的援助(“公共安全网家庭参与情况”),而不仅仅是托儿工作者本人获得的援助,且该研究并未区分劳动力中的美国公民与外国人。[181] 由于非合法永久居民的外国人通常不具备该调查所涉经济状况审查类公共福利项目的资格,因此可以合理推定,即使调查中回应的托儿工作者本人确实领取了这些福利,他们也多为美国公民,或者较少见地为合法永久居民。这些研究表明,托儿劳动力中有许多外国人,且包含托儿工作者的许多家庭至少领取一项经济状况审查类公共福利。但这些研究并未表明受公共负担可予拒绝入境理由约束的外国籍托儿工作者领取了这些福利,并会选择退出或放弃登记。关于美国移民及海关执法局(ICE)逮捕无证外国人的问题,此事不在本规则制定范围之内。
Response: DHS disagrees the final rule is ambiguous or that the removal of the 2022 Final Rule will cause child care workers to drop out of the workforce. As noted in other comment responses, DHS was clear in the NPRM and is clear in this final rule, after rescission of the 2022 Final Rule officers will be able to consider the receipt of all means-tested public benefits received by aliens subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility. DHS is clarifying that previously excluded means-tested public benefits will not be considered if received before the effective date of this final rule and that means-tested public benefits received by the alien's family members are only considered in certain circumstances related to the alien's assets, resources, and financial status. Finally, the receipt of means-tested public benefits by child care workers is one consideration in the totality of the circumstances and officers have full discretion to consider all other information and evidence relevant to public charge inadmissibility determinations. DHS neither disputes the argument that low wage child care workers receive means-tested public benefits, nor that child care workers serve an important role in the labor force. However, while this rule may cause certain aliens to forgo receiving means-tested public benefits, DHS disagrees that this rule will cause alien child care workers to drop out of the workforce; if these aliens remain in the United States, they will need to continue working in order to support themselves and their families. In addition, rather than relying on government programs to meet their needs, these aliens should rely on their own resources as well as those of their relatives, friends, or private organizations to help supplement their income. See 8 U.S.C. 1601(2)(A). Finally, DHS notes that the studies cited by the commenter concerning the child care workforce, while suggestive, do not directly support the claims made by the commenter. Specifically, the study on the percentage of immigrants in the early care and education workforce, based on American Community Survey (ACS) data, cannot distinguish between aliens who are LPRs (and therefore not subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility) and aliens who are not LPRs and may in the future seek to adjust status or be admitted to the United States (who are affected by this rule).[180] The study cited by the commenter for the claim that “43 percent of child care workers used public assistance” included assistance received by family or household members (“public safety net household participation”), not just the child care workers themselves, and did not distinguish between U.S. citizens and aliens in the workforce.[181] Since aliens who are not LPRs are generally ineligible for the means-tested public benefit programs included in the survey, it is reasonable to assume that even if the child care workers responding to the survey received those benefits themselves, they were either U.S. citizens or, less likely, LPRs. The studies show that there are many aliens in the child care workforce and that many households containing child care workers receive at least one means-tested public benefit. The studies do not show that alien child care workers subject to the public charge ground of inadmissibility receive those benefits and would choose to disenroll or forego enrollment. Regarding ICE arrests of unauthorized aliens, this is outside the scope of this rulemaking.
2. 关于明确性与歧视的担忧
2. Concerns About Clarity and Discrimination
a. 缺乏明确的定义和标准
a. Lack of Clear Definitions and Standards
评论意见:一位评论者询问,在废止2022年最终规则与实施任何新政策之间(印刷页第45371页),是否会有任何过渡性标准来规范国土安全部所作出的决定。
Comment: A commenter asked whether any interim standard would govern decisions made by DHS between ( printed page 45371) rescission of the 2022 Final Rule and implementation of any new policy.
答复:不,国土安全部(DHS)不会实施过渡性标准。该法规要求国土安全部考虑申请人的年龄、健康状况、家庭状况、资产、资源和财务状况,以及教育和技能。国土安全部还认为,国会意图要求官员考虑申请入境或调整身份的外国人是否曾领取经济状况调查类公共福利。数十年来一直指导公共负担不可入境性认定且至今仍为有效法律依据的判例决定规定,国土安全部官员还应考虑他们认为与在所有情况综合考量下判断该外国人是否可能在任何时候成为公共负担相关的任何其他因素和信息,这正是国会的意图。[182]因此,寻求以移民和非移民身份入境的外国人以及申请调整身份的外国人应当预期,其案件中存在的任何与其成为公共负担可能性相关的事实或情况都将被国土安全部纳入考量。
Response: No, DHS is not implementing an interim standard. The statute requires DHS to consider an applicant's age, health, family status, assets, resources and financial status, and education and skills. DHS also believes Congress intended officers to consider any receipt of means-tested public benefits by the alien applying for admission or adjustment of status. Precedent decisions that have guided public charge inadmissibility determinations for decades and remain good law today dictate that DHS officers consider as well as any other factors and information they find relevant to determining whether the alien is likely at any time to become a public charge in the totality of the circumstances, as Congress intended.[182] Therefore, aliens seeking admission as immigrants and nonimmigrants and aliens applying for adjustment of status should expect any fact or circumstance present in their case that is relevant to their likelihood of becoming a public charge will be considered by DHS.
评论:一位评论者建议国土安全部提供更多细节,说明哪些特征会导致某人被视为“在任何时候都可能成为公共负担”,并列出哪些因素被视为较弱或情境性因素。
Comment: One commenter recommended DHS provide more details on characteristics that would lead one to be considered “likely at any time to become a public charge,” and outline those treated as weaker or contextual factors.
答复:国土安全部拒绝对任何特定因素赋予具体权重,因为公共负担不可入境性认定是一项主观的、酌情的、个案具体的认定。在每一个案件中,国土安全部都将基于评估外国人的年龄、健康状况、家庭状况、资产、资源和财务状况,以及教育和技能、该外国人领取任何经济状况调查类公共福利的情况,以及国土安全部官员认定与评估该个别外国人在任何时候成为公共负担可能性相关的任何其他因素,作出决定。国土安全部认为,鉴于认定某外国人在任何时候可能成为公共负担的情况会因个案事实而异,提供狭义的概要来详细说明哪些因素会导致如此认定将与判例决定不一致。[183]鉴于国土安全部有意保留官员的自由裁量权,且此类认定具有高度的个案具体性,国土安全部拒绝对与公共负担不可入境性认定相关的任何因素或情况规定价值或赋予权重。
Response: DHS declines to attach specific weight to any particular factor because the public charge inadmissibility determination is a subjective, discretionary, and case-specific determination. In every case, DHS will make a determination based on assessing the alien's age, health, family status, assets, resources, and financial status, and education and skills, the alien's receipt of any means-tested public benefits, and any other factors the DHS officer determines are relevant to assessing that individual alien's likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge. DHS believes it would be inconsistent with precedent decisions to provide a narrow outline detailing what makes an alien likely at any time to become a public charge given it varies depending on the facts of an individual alien's case.[183] DHS declines to prescribe value or attribute weight to any factors or circumstances relevant to public charge inadmissibility determinations given DHS's interest in preserving officer discretion and the highly fact-specific nature of such determinations.
如果评论者关心的是外国人提供裁决所需信息的能力,国土安全部指出,外国人可以提供他们认为有助于证明自己在任何时候都不太可能成为公共负担的任何信息。此外,官员可在适当情况下发出补充证据请求(RFE)或拟拒绝通知(NOID)。
If the commenter's concern is about an alien's ability to provide the information needed for adjudication, DHS notes that aliens may provide any information they believe relevant in demonstrating they are not likely at any time to become a public charge. Furthermore, officers may issue an RFE or NOID when appropriate.
评论:评论者称国土安全部正在用含糊的语言和标准取代透明的法规,其中一位建议国土安全部扩大8 CFR 212.22(a)项下官员可考虑的因素范围,以解决拟议规则制定通知(NPRM)中所指出的问题,而不是让该法规的适用对官员而言含糊不清、未作明确界定,其他评论者则表示将缺乏明确的定义和标准。
Comment: Commenters stated DHS is replacing transparent regulations with vague language and standards, with one suggesting DHS expand the factors officers can consider under 8 CFR 212.22(a) to address the concerns identified in the NPRM, rather than leaving the application of the statute vague and undefined for officers while others stated there would be a lack of clear definitions and standards.
答复:国土安全部并非要取代2022年最终规则,而是废止并删除了存在问题的2022年最终规则,从而确保国土安全部官员作出的公共负担不可入境性认定符合《移民与国籍法》(INA)第212(a)(4)条,即8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)、《个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)以及数十年来一直指导公共负担不可入境性认定的既往判例决定。90 FR 52168, 52184(2025年11月19日)。删除相关法规使国土安全部官员能够根据国会意图作出准确、精确的公共负担不可入境性认定。90 FR 52168, 52168(2025年11月19日)。根据本规则,国土安全部官员不仅有权考虑法定强制因素、经济状况调查类公共福利的领取情况,以及记录中有关该外国人已申请或已被批准或核准领取任何经济状况调查类公共福利的任何证据,还有权考虑官员认定与评估个别外国人在任何时候成为公共负担可能性相关的任何其他个案具体证据。这恢复了一项信任并依赖国土安全部官员健全判断和自由裁量权的公共负担不可入境性认定机制,正如国会制定《移民与国籍法》第212(a)(4)条,即8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)时所设想的那样。
Response: DHS is not replacing the 2022 Final Rule. Rather, DHS rescinded and removed the problematic 2022 Final Rule, which ensures DHS officers make public charge inadmissibility determinations consistent with section 212(a)(4) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182 (a)(4), PRWORA, and past precedent decisions that have guided public charge inadmissibility determinations for decades. 90 FR 52168, 52184 (Nov. 19, 2025). Removing regulations enables DHS officers to make accurate and precise public charge inadmissibility determinations, consistent with congressional intent. 90 FR 52168, 52168 (Nov. 19, 2025). Under this rule, DHS officers will be empowered to consider not only mandatory statutory factors, receipt of means-tested public benefits, and any evidence in the record the alien applied for or has been approved or certified to receive any means-tested public benefits, but also any other case-specific evidence that the officer determines is relevant to assessing an individual alien's likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge. This restores a public charge inadmissibility determination that trusts in and relies on DHS officers' sound judgment and discretion, as envisioned by Congress when it enacted section 212(a)(4) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4).
DHS指出,申请调整身份的外国人可以随时提交他们认为与评估其自给自足能力及未来成为公共负担可能性相关的任何证据。因此,外国人将有充分机会向美国公民及移民服务局(USCIS)提供有关其未来成为公共负担可能性的完整背景信息。
DHS notes aliens applying for adjustment of status may submit any evidence they feel is relevant to assessing their self-sufficiency and likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge. As such, aliens will have ample opportunity to provide USCIS with the full context surrounding their likelihood at any time of becoming a public charge.
DHS认为,遵循《移民与国籍法》(INA)第212(a)(4)条(载于8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4))以及《个人责任与工作机会协调法》(PRWORA)中所确立的国会意图,并不会导致公共负担不可入境性政策含糊不清,因为该法规及数十年的判例均明确规定,官员必须适用综合情况考量方法。就该法规要求在公共负担不可入境性认定中考虑一份非穷尽式因素清单而言,DHS认为,这表明国会意图在每一项个别认定中为官员保留自由裁量的空间。INA第212(a)(4)(B)条,8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(B)。
DHS does not believe that following congressional intent, as set forth in section 212(a)(4) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4), and PRWORA, leads to a vague public charge inadmissibility policy because the statute and decades of precedent are clear that officers must apply the totality of the circumstances approach. To the extent that the statute includes a requirement to consider a non-exhaustive list of factors in public charge inadmissibility determinations, DHS believes that this is evidence that Congress intended to leave room for officer discretion in each individual determination. INA sec. 212(a)(4)(B), 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4)(B).
b. 关于偏见与歧视的担忧
b. Concerns About Bias and Discrimination
Comment: Commenters stated that rescinding the 2022 Final Rule and restoring broad undefined public charge inadmissibility determinations increases the risk of bias or discrimination influencing decisions about immigration benefits. Another commenter stated that discretionary standards frequently result in unequal treatment and ( printed page 45372) discrimination. A commenter expressed concern that public charge inadmissibility determinations are “necessarily subjective,” writing such an approach is untenable as it opens the door to bias and abuse.
Response: These commenters failed to explain how public charge inadmissibility determinations under this final rule will result in discriminatory or unequal application. Regardless, DHS disagrees that the final rule increases the risk that bias or discrimination will influence public charge inadmissibility determinations. Additionally, as noted in previous comment responses, DHS strongly disagrees that the rule is vague or will result in discrimination or unequal treatment to any specific group.
The public charge inadmissibility determination has always been inherently discretionary and necessarily subjective due to its prospective nature. DHS believes that the precedent decisions that have guided public charge inadmissibility determinations for decades, as well as applicable recent circuit case law, provide officers with sufficient guidance to make individualized, case-specific public charge inadmissibility determinations that are not biased or discriminatory. Under this rulemaking, DHS officers will consider the statutorily-mandated factors as well as any other factors relevant to determining whether any individual alien is likely at any time to become a public charge, including the alien's applications, approvals or certifications to receive, or receipt of means-tested public benefits, in the totality of the circumstances as Congress intended. While officers will be able to consider any individualized, case-specific factors, circumstances, and empirical data rather than being forced to ignore evidence that falls outside of the narrow regulatory requirements, such factors, circumstances, and data must be relevant to the prospective public charge inadmissibility determination. The evidence considered by USCIS may be different from that which is considered by CBP, due to operational limitations at and between ports of entry. Factors and information that are irrelevant to the determination or that relate to protected classes are not to be considered by officers. Explicit regulatory language is not required to prevent officers from considering these factors and such language was never a part of public charge regulations.
As to the research one commenter points to suggesting that discretion in public benefits programs frequently results in unequal treatment and discrimination, this commenter did not cite any authorities or studies in support of the contention. Separately, DHS notes the commenter did not include examples of public charge inadmissibility being applied unequally or in a discriminatory fashion.
Comment: Many commenters stated that the proposed rule is broad and vague, which will risk or result in a discriminatory and biased application of the ground of inadmissibility. Another commenter wrote that the removal of existing regulatory content relating to the statutory minimum factors found in 8 CFR 212.22(a)(1) would lead to discriminatory, arbitrary, and capricious results. Other commenters noted that expanding discretion without clear standards invites implicit bias by officers making racialized assumptions about self-sufficiency, resulting in unequal treatment. Another commenter noted that the NPRM's broad discretionary model effectively resurrects policy tools historically used to exclude, stigmatize, and marginalize immigrant communities, which is out of step with USCIS' obligations to administer immigration law fairly, equitably, and without discrimination. A commenter stated that research on the implementation of other public programs demonstrates that discretionary standards frequently result in unequal treatment and discrimination. One commenter wrote that in the requirement for officers to conduct a “totality of the circumstances” test, weighing factors such as age, health, and financial status, grants broad discretion could lead to subjective and potentially discriminatory outcomes, thereby undermining the principle of fair and uniform application of immigration law.
Response: It is unclear how these commenters believe public charge inadmissibility determinations under this rule will result in discriminatory or unequal application, to whom this rule will be biased against, and what assumptions will be made about self-sufficiency. However, DHS strongly disagrees that this rule is vague or will result in discrimination or unequal treatment to any specific group. The Federal Government is responsible for “regulating the relationship between the United States and our alien visitors,” which includes regulating the manner and conditions of entry, as well as the residence of aliens.[184] DHS is the Federal agency with the authority to establish regulations regarding the admission, and therefore, admissibility of aliens.[185] Section 212(a) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a), sets forth the aliens who are inadmissible and therefore ineligible for visas, admission, or adjustment of status. Section 212(a)(4) of the INA, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4), sets forth the aliens who are inadmissible under the public charge ground of inadmissibility and the minimum factors DHS is required to consider in the public charge inadmissibility analysis. DHS must consider an applicant's age, health, family status, assets, resources and financial status, and education and skills. Under this rulemaking, DHS officers will consider any other factors they determine are relevant to determining whether any individual alien is self-sufficient, as Congress intended,[186] and whether the alien is likely at any time to become a public charge in the totality of the circumstances.
DHS also notes that to the extent these commenters are concerned that the focus on self-sufficiency will disproportionately impact low-income aliens, DHS notes that an alien's income is not outcome-determinative. As dictated by the statute and binding precedent decisions that have guided these determinations for decades, DHS will consider all relevant factors in the totality of the circumstances. Under this determination, aliens seeking admission as immigrants and nonimmigrants and aliens applying for adjustment of status should expect that any fact present in their case that is relevant to their self-sufficiency and likelihood of becoming a public charge will be considered by DHS.
While DHS cannot completely eliminate the possibility of officer bias or racialized assumptions about self-sufficiency, USCIS will provide training to officers and will issue guidance on all aspects of these determinations, which should help ameliorate any concerns that the public charge inadmissibility ground would be unequally applied to different groups of aliens. Additionally, with respect to adjustment of status applications adjudicated by USCIS, in order to ensure that USCIS officers are making clear, fair, and consistent public charge inadmissibility determinations, as required in existing regulations, USCIS officers will issue written decisions that reflect every factor considered and articulate the reasons for the officer's determination. 8 CFR 103.3(a)(1)(i).
Comment: Some commenters stated that this rule is being used to push a ( printed page 45373) racist, xenophobic, and anti-immigration agenda with one commenter stating it is part of a “racist, xenophobic, [w]hite supremacist” plan to eliminate all immigration, legal and otherwise, to the United States. The commenter stated that the United States needs more immigrants, not fewer, and urged DHS to keep the 1999 Interim Field Guidance and reject the proposed change in its entirety.
Response: DHS disagrees that public charge inadmissibility determinations that will be made under this final rule are discriminatory, anti-immigration, or racially motivated. The purpose of the public charge ground of inadmissibility is not to ensure that more aliens are able to be admitted to the United States or adjust status to that of an LPR, but rather, like all grounds of inadmissibility, to prevent certain aliens from entering or remaining in the United States.[187]
To the extent that public charge inadmissibility determinations under this final rule may result in more aliens being found inadmissible, this is a natural byproduct of robust enforcement of immigration laws that are meant to minimize the incentive of aliens to immigrate to the United States due to the availability of public benefits and to promote the self-sufficiency of aliens within the United States. 8 U.S.C. 1601(1) and (2). However, if rescission of the 2022 Final Rule impacts certain groups more than others, that simply is not DHS's intent.
